label: Scope of the Cartesian containment clause: respect-wise versus whole-effect
term: containment clause (whatever is in the effect is in its total cause)
resolution: The clause is kept as two sibling statements, one per scope. CONTAINMENT_SCOPE_1 (respect-wise) constrains the total cause of each perfection; CONTAINMENT_SCOPE_2 (whole-effect) constrains the total cause of a thing's being in every perfection of the thing. q.4 a.2 preexistence entails the whole-effect reading (a strength order); on the respect-wise reading, preexistence and containment are independent (two finite controls). No argument passes between the two scopes; an argument using both would need an explicit bridge such as the cause-of-being transfer f8ba2429-b4f1-5712-a4d3-798213963d34. Both readings use one uniform InAct (IN_ACT_4) on both sides; the mode-asymmetric reading (formal in the effect, formal or eminent in the cause) is a further, unformalized sibling.
